paul_devex: Heads up — a dev on Windows (WSL2) hit TLS verify fails when calling the hosted API: `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`. Happens in Node (fetch/axios) and curl inside WSL. Anyone seen this with corporate MITM proxies + WSL?

arin_eng: Yep seen that. Usually the corp proxy injects its own root CA but the process inside WSL isn't picking up the Windows cert store. WSL distro might be using Alpine or a Debian image without the corp cert installed.

maya_sre: Quick checklist: 1) check the chain with openssl, 2) verify which CA store your runtime uses (OpenSSL vs NSS vs system store), 3) try curl with `--cacert` to confirm it's a trust-store issue.

paul_devex: logs from the app: `FetchError: request to https://api.redwood.com/ failed, reason: self signed certificate in certificate chain`. Running `curl https://api.redwood.com -v` inside WSL gives `SSL: certificate subject name 'Corp Proxy' does not match` and also shows the proxy cert.

jasmin_mac: Commands that helped me debug on WSL: 
```
# inspect the presented cert chain
openssl s_client -showcerts -servername api.redwood.com -connect api.redwood.com:443
# test curl with the corp CA bundle
curl --cacert /mnt/c/Users/jasmin/certs/corp-root.pem https://api.redwood.com -v
```

arin_eng: Fix options (ordered by quick -> proper):
- Quick env override (Node/Python): `export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/corp-root.pem` or for requests: `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corp-root.pem`
- For Docker containers: bake the corp cert into the image or mount it and update the distro CA store (Debian/Ubuntu: copy to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` then `sudo update-ca-certificates`).
- For Go apps: `crypto/x509.SystemCertPool()` on musl can be flaky; recommend bundling the PEM or use `SSL_CERT_FILE` in the container.

paul_devex: We're shipping SDKs — any recommended pattern to make this smoother for folks behind proxies?

maya_sre: Good patterns we use in other SDKs:
- Honor `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `SSL_CERT_FILE` environment vars and document them in quickstart.
- Expose a `REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE` env var as well so customers can set app-level CA without clobbering system env in shared environments.
- Provide a helper script `scripts/install-corp-ca.sh` for common OSes (WSL, macOS, Debian) that: imports the cert, updates store, and prints one-liners. Link to internal doc: https://redwood.internal/devex/tls-wsl-proxy (draft).

arin_eng: For Node-specific SDK code, we added an optional constructor param `caPath` that does: 
```
const ca = fs.readFileSync(caPath);
const agent = new https.Agent({ ca });
fetch(url, { agent });
```
That avoids relying on OpenSSL env quirks and works inside containers.

jasmin_mac: One odd gotcha: on macOS people import corp cert into Keychain but Node (homebrew) sometimes still uses OpenSSL's store. On mac, use `security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain corp-root.pem` and then restart apps.

maya_sre: Also watch for client cert (mTLS) cases: if a customer supplies a client key + cert, ensure perms are `600` and that the process can read them. In Docker mounts the mode can be 000 — that causes silent failures.

cert-rot-bot: Reminder: next client cert rotation window is 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Ensure automation pulls new PKCS12 and writes `client.pem` and `client.key` with 600 perms.

paul_devex: One last weird one — WSL1/2 symlink weirdness made `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/mnt/c/...` unreadable by some processes. Solution was copying the PEM into the distro filesystem (`/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp.crt`) then `sudo update-ca-certificates`.

arin_eng: TL;DR troubleshooting steps for folks who file tickets:
1) `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <host>:443` -> confirm proxy cert.
2) `curl --cacert /path/to/corp.pem <host>` -> confirm trust with bundle.
3) try `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` in app process.
4) if inside container, add cert to image or mount and update distro CA store.
5) if using mTLS, check key permissions and PKCS12 conversion: `openssl pkcs12 -in client.p12 -out client.pem -nodes`.

paul_devex: Thanks all — I pushed a small README update to the SDK repo with the env var notes and the WSL one-liners. Testing now — will ping when QA confirms. :thumbsup:

jasmin_mac: tested locally after copying cert into distro store, everything green. :party:

paul_devex: Awesome, closing the loop. If anyone wants the `install-corp-ca.sh` skeleton ping me and I'll open a PR.
